author: AI Editorial Team (Esi)
key_learning_objective: Apply the safety check required before administering digoxin.
question_stem: Before administering digoxin to a client with heart failure, the nurse assesses an apical heart rate of 52 beats/min. What is the appropriate action?

options.B: Hold the dose and notify the provider
options.D: Administer the dose and recheck the pulse in 1 hour

rationales.A: Giving digoxin with a heart rate below 60 beats/min can worsen bradycardia and may signal toxicity.
rationales.B: Correct. Digoxin is withheld when the apical pulse is < 60 beats/min (adult); the nurse holds the dose and notifies the provider.
rationales.C: Nurses do not independently alter the prescribed dose.
rationales.D: The drug should not be given first; the low rate is the reason to hold.

key_takeaway: Check apical pulse for a full minute before digoxin. Hold if < 60 bpm (adult) and notify the provider.
nclex_test_taking_tip: Nurses never invent a dose (rules out 'give half'). Safety check first.
memory_trick: Dig + pulse under 60 = don't dig in.
clinical_pearls: Assess apical pulse for a full 60 seconds.
Early digoxin toxicity: anorexia, nausea, visual halos; hypokalemia worsens it.
